messages:
maria: Heads-up — seeing multiple GPU attach failures in eu-central tonight. Nodes get auto-evicted because the local NVMe is being flagged with transient "bad block" events, but SMART/SMARTCTL looks fine. Any ideas? dmesg excerpt below.

maria: ```
[02:11:03] nvme0n1: bad block reported at LBA 0x00000000000001f4
[02:11:03] nvme0: Reset controller due to media error
[02:11:04] nvme0n1: I/O error, dev fsync failed
[02:11:04] kernel: nvme_core: failed to flush: -5
```

jon: which nodes exactly? preemptible or dedicated?

maria: gn-ec-1824, gn-ec-1830, gn-ec-1841 — all preemptible. ops-bot had auto-evict triggers for each.

ops-bot: Auto-evict: node gn-ec-1824 triggered (reason: nvme.badblock_count > threshold). Grace window started.

liam: this pattern looks odd — reminds me of the cleaner vs snapshot race we saw but not identical. Can you paste last janitor/scrub entries for those nodes?

maria: ```
/var/log/janitor.log:
02:10:58 scrub-start gn-ec-1824 namespace ephemeral scrub id=993
02:11:01 scrub-write 32MB chunk id=993 offset=0x1f0
02:11:02 scrub-complete partial id=993 err=EIO
```

alex: quick thought — could be a transient metadata write interrupted by network flaps. I vaguely recall nvme drivers flagging blocks if underlying write completions don't make it back. Any peering noise in eu-central around 02:05-02:12?

sre-bot: Correlation scan: 14 nodes with nvme.badblock events had a network peering jitter at 02:07 UTC (upstream ASN 64512). Confidence: medium.

sam: We had an upstream BGP jitter at ~02:06 due to a partial route flap, ops ticket #INC-3872. That caused short API/connectivity hiccups to control plane in eu-central.

jon: If network partitions interrupted background write paths (e.g., janitor, scrub, snapshot), the NVMe controller might see incomplete metadata transactions and mark a block. Not necessarily physical corruption.

maria: Agreed. For now I disabled aggressive scrubs in eu-central and bumped the gpu-attach retry window from 30s -> 120s to avoid immediate evictions while we triage. Rolling out change now.

security: Any risk of unreadable user data? SMART params look stable and remap_count hasn't increased. From initial glance this looks like false-positive badblock flags rather than actual media failure.

liam: Action items: 1) collect nvme id-ctrl + smartctl -a for each affected node (I/O + firmware versions). 2) reproduce a controlled network partition in the lab while running a scrub to see if we can trigger the same flagging. 3) consider reverting yesterday's kernel rollout in eu-central if repro is fast. 4) open vendor firmware ticket if we can't reproduce. I'll take lab repro.

maria: I'll attach the nvme id-ctrl outputs to the incident and tag you. Also going to backfill a short-lived capacity buffer in eu-central (reserve ~30 instances) so product doesn't hit GPU attach SLOs if this continues — finance FYI, that could be ~10k/mo in transient cost. :money_with_wings: tagging @finance.

jon: If mitigation reduces evict churn we probably don't need the full buffer, but good call to have a short-lived commit.

alex: Long-term we may need an adaptive evict policy that can distinguish metadata-flap badblocks vs persistent media faults. For now the less-risky path is throttle janitor scrubs during peering instability windows.

maria: Thanks all. I'll post a follow-up in 30m with updated metrics and a list of affected firmware/kernel variants. If anyone wants live access to gn-ec-1824 before we reattach, ping me. :thumbsup:
